message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and news, then bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$9,812 total — within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, funded entirely from the $50,000 cash balance with no money moved out of the account). The limit was set just above the current quote of $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), so it was close to market. The decision rested on Apple's fiscal Q4/FY2024 results reported October 31 and filed in its 10-K on November 1: quarterly revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and full-year revenue of $391.0B, operating income of $123.2B, net income of $93.7B, diluted EPS of $6.08 (including a one-time $10.2B tax charge), and operating cash flow of $118.3B — a business still growing with very strong cash generation and margins. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were roughly flat around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, which leaves a potential upgrade-cycle catalyst ahead without an obvious negative surprise. Given the modest growth rate and the fact that the stock is not cheaply valued, I sized the position at the low end of the mandate rather than the maximum, keeping the rest of the daily budget available.
message.reasoning:
Order filled at 223.00, 44 shares = $9,812. Under $10k per order, under $20k total today. Cash was $50,000, so no money moved out.

Summarize.
